regions.breakdown: パン (pan) - bread (loanword); と (to) - and; 和洋菓子 (wayougashi) - Japanese (和, wa) and Western (洋, you) confectionery (菓子, gashi).
小尾 (Obi) - a family name; ベーカリー (beekarii) - bakery (loanword).

regions.original: この夏、絶対当たる！ サントリー飲料 2022年夏の絶対もらえるキャンペーン
regions.translation: This summer, definitely win! Suntory Beverages Summer 2022 'Absolutely Get' Campaign
regions.romanization: Kono natsu, zettai ataru! Santorii inryou nisen-nijuuni-nen natsu no zettai moraeru kyanpeen
regions.breakdown: この夏 (kono natsu) - this summer; 絶対 (zettai) - absolutely, definitely; 当たる (ataru) - to hit, to win (a prize); サントリー飲料 (Santorii inryou) - Suntory Beverages; 2022年 (nisen-nijuuni-nen) - year 2022; 夏 (natsu) - summer; の (no) - possessive particle; 絶対もらえる (zettai moraeru) - absolutely get; キャンペーン (kyanpeen) - campaign (loanword).

where_youd_see_it: On a shop sign and vending machine in a Japanese street.
cultural_note: Vending machines are ubiquitous in Japan, offering a wide variety of drinks. Many bakeries and confectionery shops in Japan offer both traditional Japanese sweets (wagashi) and Western-style pastries (yogashi).
